# Scouts (Éclaireur / hunter)

## In short
- **Camouflage lets you walk through zones you don't control.** A Scout wearing an active Camouflage Vest (`vest_on_#00`) can leave a zone that zombies control.
- **Each move can get you spotted.** When you enter a zone with more zombies than control points (CP), there is a chance you are spotted and lose your camouflage. The chance grows with the zombie surplus. It is lower at night and drops by 3 points per scout level of the zone you enter.
- **Other actions break camouflage for certain.** In an uncontrolled zone with no escape timer, picking up or dropping items, clearing debris, searching a building, or using actions and recipes that don't keep cover always breaks it.
- **Scout visits build up zone scout levels.** Every move a Scout makes leaves a permanent visit marker. Every 5 markers on a zone add 1 scout level, up to 3. Each level adds +2.5% to digging chances, and at level 2 or higher a Scout's zombie estimate is exact. The Scouts' Lair only makes these markings visible on the map.

## How it works

### Camouflage and movement
- **When you can move.** Normally you can't leave a zone you don't control unless you have an escape timer. Carrying `vest_on_#00` lifts this block [1]. The check runs for every mover, escorts included. Any mover who has no vest and no escape timer blocks the whole move [1].
- **Putting the vest on.** The Camouflage action (`hero_hunter_1`/`hero_hunter_2`) turns `vest_off_#00` into `vest_on_#00`. Outside town you need:
  - no followers;
  - a zone that is controlled or temporarily controlled ("It is impossible to use camouflage when the zone is controlled by zombies!").

  In town it has no other condition [2].
- **Starting vest.** The Scout starts with the Camouflage Vest. An alternative start gives it unequipped [3].
- **Ruins.** With an active vest a Scout can also enter an explorable ruin in a zone that zombies control [1].
- **Losing camouflage.** "Uncovering" means the vest turns back from `vest_on_#00` into `vest_off_#00` [4].

### Chance to be spotted when moving
The check runs for each mover with the Scout job who carried `vest_on_#00` when the move started. It happens only if the destination's CP are below its zombie count. Destination CP = CP of the zone (`getZoneControlPoints`) plus the CP of every mover in the group [1]:

1. `delta = floor((zombies − CP) × 1.3)`
2. At night, `delta −= 5`. Night is checked with `isNightMode(ignoreNightModeConfig: true)`, so it applies even where night mode is turned off [1]. Night is any hour before the start or after the end of the daytime range, which is [7,18] by default [5] [6].
3. If `delta ≤ 6`, it is halved.
4. `chance = max(0, delta − 3 × destination scout level) / 100`. If the roll succeeds, the vest is uncovered and you see "You were spotted by a zombie in the zone!" [1].

The scout level used here is the full zone level from step 4 of the next section, whether or not a Scouts' Lair exists [7].

Worked examples (my own arithmetic from the formula above), alone with 2 CP:

| Zombies | Time | Scout level 0 | Scout level 1 | Scout level 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Day | delta 3 → halved → 1.5% | 0% | 0% |
| 10 | Day | 10% | 7% | 1% |
| 10 | Night | delta 5 → halved → 2.5% | 0% | 0% |
| 20 | Day | 23% | 20% | 14% |
| 20 | Night | 18% | 15% | 9% |

### Other things that break camouflage (100%)
Each of these uncovers the vest for certain if the zone is not under control **and** you have no running escape timer [1]:
- using an item or heroic action that is not flagged "keeps cover";
- assembling a recipe that is not "stealthy";
- clearing debris of a buried ruin;
- searching a building.

Picking up or dropping items outside does the same, except while you are inside an explorable ruin.

### Scout visits and zone scout levels
1. **Visit markers.** On every move, each mover with the Scout job adds a `ScoutVisit` marker to the zone they enter. This happens after the spotting check and whether or not they wear the vest [1].
2. **Map markings.** The old Scout building action (type 10401) adds `ScoutMarker` markers [8]:
   - it marks 3–6 random zones that are below scout level 3;
   - between floor(n/2) and n of them are within 11 km, the rest are farther away.
3. **Markers are permanent.** Both marker types are not "daily", so the nightly cleanup keeps them [9] [10].
4. **Zone scout level.** `min(3, floor(ScoutVisit markers / 5) + ScoutMarker markers)`. It is always 0 on the town zone [7]. Visits from all citizens count together.

### Effect on digging
- **Bonus.** Desert digging gets `+0.025 × zone scout level`, so up to +7.5% at level 3. It is added after the base chance, job bonus, night malus and statuses, and it applies on depleted zones too [11].
- **Base chances.** 60% on a zone with digs left, 35% on a depleted zone [12].
- **Cap.** The final roll is limited to 10%–90% [13].
- **Not affected.** Searching ruin buildings and explorable ruins gets no scout bonus [11].
- **Uncontrolled zones.** If zombies outnumber the zone's CP, all dig timers go passive and nothing is dug. A camouflaged Scout cannot dig there [13].

### Effect on detection (zombie estimates)
- **Adjacent zones.** A Scout always sees a personal zombie estimate for the zones next to them. This does not need the Lair [14].
- **Estimate formula.** Real zombies ± an offset, never below 0. The offset is fixed per citizen and zone, with range `max(0, 2 − zone scout level)`:
  - ±2 at level 0;
  - ±1 at level 1;
  - exact at level 2 or 3;
  - an empty zone always shows 0 [7].
- **Danger level.** The adjacent zone is shown as level 2 if the estimate is ≥ 9, level 1 if it is ≥ 5, otherwise 0 [14].
- **Map discovery.** The scout level a citizen sees on the map raises their own discovery state for that zone [14]:
  - level 1–2 counts as "seen before";
  - level 3 counts as fully visible, showing the exact count if the zone's zombie status is exact, or a danger level if it is estimated.

### Scouts' Lair (`small_watchmen_#01`)
- **Cost.** Child of the Watchtower. 25 AP, 25 structure points, 0 defense, blueprint level 3 [15].
  - Default resources: 3 Metal Support, Battery, Sheet Metal, Telescope, 2 Radius Radar Beacon, Copper Pipe, 2 Twisted Plank [15].
- **Effect.** When built, it turns on the town parameter `ScoutMarkingsEnabled`. On the map this means [14]:
  - **Scouts** see the visit-based part, i.e. visits by all citizens. On the world map this is not just their own visits. A partial-progress flag appears once any visits exist.
  - **Scouts and Guides** see the "global" part: `ScoutMarker` markers plus visit markers whose citizen has been removed.
  - Shown level = the parts the viewer can see added together, capped at 3 [14].
  - In the local view next to the Scout, the visit part counts only the Scout's own visits.
- **What it doesn't change.** The spotting reduction and the dig bonus always use the full zone level, Lair or not [7] [1].
- **Beyond-page display.** The beyond page shows a Scout the visit-based level, plus the global level only if they also have the Guide role [1].

## What changes it
- **Scout job (`hunter`).** Starts with the vest. Is the only job checked for spotting and the only one that leaves visit markers. Gets the adjacent-zone estimates. Digging bonus +0% [3] [1].
- **Your group's and the zone's CP.** These lower the zombie surplus that drives the spotting chance [1] [4]:
  - base 2 CP per citizen;
  - +2 for an unbroken `shield_#00`;
  - +1 for an unbroken `defence_cp` item;
  - Guide role: + the number of citizens in the zone;
  - optional bonuses for clean, hydrated and sober;
  - `terror` sets a citizen's CP to 0.
- **Night.** −5 to delta [1].
- **Escape timer.** While one is running, items, actions, debris clearing and building searches don't break camouflage. Moving removes your escape timers [1]. When a zone loses control because someone leaves, a 30-minute grace timer is set [13].
- **Guide role.** Sees the global map markings (with the Lair) and adds the global level on the beyond page [14] [1].
- **Upgraded map (`item_electro_#00`).** Makes zone zombie counts exact, which fully visible zones then show [14].
- **Movement-stopping statuses.** `wound4` (20%) and `terror` (5%, only in a zone with zombies) can stop any move [1].
- No hero skill touching camouflage or scout levels turned up in the list of hero skills [16].

## Town types
- **Scouts' Lair resources** [15]:
  - Pandemonium (hard): 9 Metal Support, 4 Battery, 3 Sheet Metal, 2 Telescope, 6 Radius Radar Beacon, 4 Copper Pipe, 8 Twisted Plank.
  - Easy: 2 Metal Support, 1 of each of the other items.
- **Lair blueprint.** It is in the hospital level-3 blueprint lists in both default and panda rules [17] [18].
- **Small towns.** Night mode is off there [19], but the −5 night reduction to spotting still applies because it ignores that setting [5]. The digging night malus does depend on night mode.
- **Other types.** The spotting formula and scout levels are the same in every town type. Custom towns can change the daytime range and dig chance settings [6] [12].

- **Which actions keep cover.** I did not check which item actions are "keeps cover" or which recipes are "stealthy".
- **Zone CP count.** I did not read `getZoneControlPoints`, so I can't say whether it includes temporary control or only the citizens already there.
